units.title: Thomas Aquinas
units.blurb: The Summa Theologica: faith and reason brought together in one great structure of questions.

units.title: Dante and Chaucer
units.blurb: A journey through the next world, and a pilgrimage full of stories.

topics.title: Aquinas: God and Creation
topics.short: Questions about God, the five ways, creation, angels and the human soul, each answered after the objections.

topics.title: Aquinas: Happiness, Virtue and Law
topics.short: What happiness is, how habits become virtues, and the kinds of law, from eternal law to human law.

topics.title: Aquinas: Faith, Hope and Love
topics.short: The virtues of faith, hope and love, and the questions on Christ and the sacraments, as the set selects them.

topics.title: Dante: Inferno
topics.short: Lost in a dark wood, Dante follows Virgil down through the circles of Hell, where each wrong has its fitting place.

topics.title: Dante: Purgatorio
topics.short: Up the mountain of Purgatory, where souls are made new one fault at a time, to meet Beatrice.

topics.title: Dante: Paradiso
topics.short: Through the spheres of heaven to the vision of 'the love that moves the sun and the other stars.'

topics.title: Chaucer: Troilus and Criseyde
topics.short: A love story set in besieged Troy: trust, fortune and betrayal in Chaucer's longest finished poem.

topics.title: Chaucer: The Canterbury Tales
topics.short: Thirty pilgrims tell stories on the road to Canterbury: knights, millers, a nun's priest and a rooster.
